newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech gas importer initials deal with Norway's GFU.
newsitem.headline: Czech gas importer initials deal with Norway's GFU.

text.p: The Czech state natural gas importer Transgas a.s. said on Tuesday it had reached a preliminary agreement with Norway's GFU gas negotiating alliance on providing natural gas supplies to the Czech Republic.
Transgas spokeswoman Barbara Praedova told Reuters that the supplies could start next year and eventually grow to about three billion cubic metres per year.
"Transgas and GFU clarified the basic conditions for long-term supplies of Norwegian natural gas to the Czech Republic in order to cover the rising demand for natural gas," Praedova said.
She added that it would be necessary to find a solution for transportation of the gas from Norway to the Czech Republic before concrete contracts are signed.
The Czechs currently require just over nine billion cubic metres of gas per year, but the country is completely dependent on supplies from Russia.
Czech gas consumption is expected to rise to some 12-13 billion cubic metres per year by the turn of the century.
Government officials have said that partial diversification of supplies would be desirable.
Transgas is a wholly state-owned company, and the government has said it will not privatise it in the forseeable future.
GFU comprises Norway's Den Norske Stats Oljeselskap ASA (Statoil), Norsk Hydro ASA and Saga Petroleum ASA.
